questions.question: Consider human reaction-like events (species includes Homo sapiens) whose rank-0 input is a Complex. For how many such events is at least one of the event's own catalyst-activity physical entities also a part of that same rank-0 input complex, where 'part of' means reachable from the complex by following hasComponent links out of complexes and hasMember links out of entity sets, to any depth?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE r0 AS (SELECT i.DB_ID AS ev, i.input AS cx FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i JOIN Complex c ON c.DB_ID = i.input JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = i.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' WHERE i.input_rank = 0), parts AS (SELECT r0.ev, hc.hasComponent AS ent FROM r0 JOIN Complex_2_hasComponent hc ON hc.DB_ID = r0.cx UNION SELECT p.ev, hc.hasComponent FROM parts p JOIN Complex_2_hasComponent hc ON hc.DB_ID = p.ent UNION SELECT p.ev, hm.hasMember FROM parts p JOIN EntitySet_2_hasMember hm ON hm.DB_ID = p.ent) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rc.DB_ID) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity rc JOIN CatalystActivity ca ON ca.DB_ID = rc.catalystActivity JOIN parts p ON p.ev = rc.DB_ID AND p.ent = ca.physicalEntity;

questions.question: Restrict to human reaction-like events (species includes Homo sapiens) that have at least 4 distinct input entities, ignoring rank and ignoring any entity listed more than once. How many unordered pairs of two different such events have exactly the same set of input entities?

queries.sql: WITH inp AS (SELECT DISTINCT i.DB_ID AS ev, i.input AS ent FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = i.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens'), card AS (SELECT ev, COUNT(*) AS n FROM inp GROUP BY ev HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM card a JOIN card b ON b.n = a.n AND b.ev > a.ev WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inp x WHERE x.ev = a.ev AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inp y WHERE y.ev = b.ev AND y.ent = x.ent));

questions.question: Human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) carry summations, and those summations cite literature references, which in turn have authors. Which people are an author of the greatest number of distinct literature references reached that way? Give the display name of every person tied for the greatest number.

queries.sql: WITH tally AS (SELECT pa.author AS person, COUNT(DISTINCT sl.literatureReference) AS n FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN Event_2_summation s ON s.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN Summation_2_literatureReference sl ON sl.DB_ID = s.summation JOIN Publication_2_author pa ON pa.DB_ID = sl.literatureReference GROUP BY pa.author) SELECT d._displayName FROM tally t JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = t.person WHERE t.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM tally);

questions.question: Consider human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) that have been reviewed, where at least one author of a reviewing InstanceEdit is affiliated with an organisation whose name contains the word 'University'. How many of those pathways directly contain, through hasEvent, an event carrying a negative preceding event whose reason has the display name 'Futile Cycle'?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pw.DB_ID) FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN Event_2_reviewed rv ON rv.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN InstanceEdit_2_author ia ON ia.DB_ID = rv.reviewed JOIN Person_2_affiliation pa ON pa.DB_ID = ia.author JOIN Affiliation_2_name an ON an.DB_ID = pa.affiliation AND an.name LIKE '%University%' JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN Event_2_negativePrecedingEvent ne ON ne.DB_ID = he.hasEvent JOIN NegativePrecedingEvent np ON np.DB_ID = ne.negativePrecedingEvent JOIN DatabaseObject rn ON rn.DB_ID = np.reason AND rn._displayName = 'Futile Cycle';

questions.question: Consider the pathways that are direct hasEvent children of the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256. For each such child, collect every event in its own hasEvent subtree including itself, take every input and output of those events, then expand any complexes through hasComponent and any entity sets through hasMember to any depth. Among the EntityWithAccessionedSequence instances found that way, which child has the greatest number of distinct reference gene products? Give the child's display name.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE roots AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS root FROM DatabaseObject d JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = d.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = d.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256'), tree AS (SELECT root, root AS ev FROM roots UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM tree t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), parts AS (SELECT t.root, i.input AS ent FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i ON i.DB_ID = t.ev UNION SELECT t.root, o.output FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_output o ON o.DB_ID = t.ev UNION SELECT p.root, hc.hasComponent FROM parts p JOIN Complex_2_hasComponent hc ON hc.DB_ID = p.ent UNION SELECT p.root, hm.hasMember FROM parts p JOIN EntitySet_2_hasMember hm ON hm.DB_ID = p.ent) SELECT d._displayName FROM parts p JOIN EntityWithAccessionedSequence e ON e.DB_ID = p.ent JOIN ReferenceGeneProduct rgp ON rgp.DB_ID = e.referenceEntity JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = p.root GROUP BY p.root, d._displayName ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT e.referenceEntity) DESC LIMIT 1;

questions.question: Call a compartment 'membrane-derived' if it reaches the GO cellular component with accession 0016020 by following one or more instanceOf links. How many human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) that directly contain at least one reaction-like event through hasEvent have every one of their directly contained reaction-like events assigned at least one membrane-derived compartment?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE anc AS (SELECT DISTINCT rc.compartment AS node, rc.compartment AS root FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc UNION SELECT i.instanceOf, a.root FROM anc a JOIN GO_CellularComponent_2_instanceOf i ON i.DB_ID = a.node), memb AS (SELECT DISTINCT a.root AS cmp FROM anc a JOIN GO_CellularComponent g ON g.DB_ID = a.node AND g.accession = '0016020') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT he.DB_ID) FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent h2 JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r2 ON r2.DB_ID = h2.hasEvent WHERE h2.DB_ID = he.DB_ID AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc JOIN memb m ON m.cmp = rc.compartment WHERE rc.DB_ID = h2.hasEvent));

questions.question: How many distinct reaction-like events lie in the hasEvent hierarchy at any depth below the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 but not at any depth below the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-392499?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE a AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev FROM DatabaseObject d JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = d.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = d.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent FROM a JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = a.ev), b AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev FROM DatabaseObject d JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = d.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = d.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-392499' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent FROM b JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = b.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = a.ev WHERE a.ev NOT IN (SELECT ev FROM b);

questions.question: How many distinct reaction-like events are regulated by a regulation whose regulator is a Complex that contains, by following hasComponent out of complexes and hasMember out of entity sets for one or more steps, a physical entity that is also the catalyst of that very same event? The regulator complex being itself the catalyst does not count; at least one containment step is required.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE regcx AS (SELECT rb.DB_ID AS ev, g.regulator AS cx FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy rb JOIN Regulation g ON g.DB_ID = rb.regulatedBy JOIN Complex c ON c.DB_ID = g.regulator), parts AS (SELECT r.ev, hc.hasComponent AS ent FROM regcx r JOIN Complex_2_hasComponent hc ON hc.DB_ID = r.cx UNION SELECT p.ev, hc.hasComponent FROM parts p JOIN Complex_2_hasComponent hc ON hc.DB_ID = p.ent UNION SELECT p.ev, hm.hasMember FROM parts p JOIN EntitySet_2_hasMember hm ON hm.DB_ID = p.ent) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ev) FROM parts p JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity rc ON rc.DB_ID = p.ev JOIN CatalystActivity ca ON ca.DB_ID = rc.catalystActivity AND ca.physicalEntity = p.ent;

questions.question: How many human complexes (species includes Homo sapiens) that have at least one direct component have every one of their direct components be an EntityWithAccessionedSequence?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT hc.DB_ID FROM Complex_2_hasComponent hc JOIN Complex_2_species cs ON cs.DB_ID = hc.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = cs.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' LEFT JOIN EntityWithAccessionedSequence e ON e.DB_ID = hc.hasComponent GROUP BY hc.DB_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT hc.hasComponent) = COUNT(DISTINCT e.DB_ID)) t;

questions.question: Consider every human pathway (species includes Homo sapiens). For each, count the distinct reaction-like events anywhere in its hasEvent subtree, and the percentage of those events having at least one catalyst activity. Return the five pathways with the most such events, ordered by that count descending and then by pathway name. Use columns named pathway, events and pct, with pct rounded to one decimal place.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS root, he.hasEvent AS ev FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), rle AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, t.ev FROM t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev), agg AS (SELECT root, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity c WHERE c.DB_ID = rle.ev) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wc FROM rle GROUP BY root) SELECT d._displayName AS pathway, a.n AS events, ROUND(100 * a.wc / a.n, 1) AS pct FROM agg a JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = a.root ORDER BY a.n DESC, pathway LIMIT 5;

questions.question: How many distinct reaction-like events are regulated by at least one regulation that is an instance of PositiveRegulation or of any subclass of PositiveRegulation, and by no regulation that is an instance of NegativeRegulation or of any subclass of NegativeRegulation?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.DB_ID) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy a JOIN PositiveRegulation pr ON pr.DB_ID = a.regulatedBy WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy b JOIN NegativeRegulation nr ON nr.DB_ID = b.regulatedBy WHERE b.DB_ID = a.DB_ID);

questions.question: For each human pathway (species includes Homo sapiens), count the distinct reaction-like events in its hasEvent subtree at any depth, considering only pathways whose subtree contains at least one. How many of those pathways have a count strictly greater than the mean count across all of them?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS root, he.hasEvent AS ev FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), agg AS (SELECT t.root, COUNT(DISTINCT t.ev) AS n FROM t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev GROUP BY t.root) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agg WHERE n > (SELECT AVG(n) FROM agg);

questions.question: Consider human reaction-like events (species includes Homo sapiens) that carry at least one regulation. What percentage of them carry no regulation that is an instance of NegativeRegulation or any of its subclasses? Round to one decimal place.

queries.sql: SELECT ROUND(100 * SUM(pos_only) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM (SELECT rb.DB_ID AS ev, MAX(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy b JOIN NegativeRegulation nr ON nr.DB_ID = b.regulatedBy WHERE b.DB_ID = rb.DB_ID) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS pos_only FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_regulatedBy rb JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = rb.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' GROUP BY rb.DB_ID) t;

questions.question: Consider the EntityWithAccessionedSequence instances that are the physical entity of a catalyst activity of some reaction-like event. How many distinct reference entities do they reference whose own reference sequence records its species as Homo sapiens? Judge the species from the reference sequence itself, not from the species of any event.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.referenceEntity) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity rc JOIN CatalystActivity ca ON ca.DB_ID = rc.catalystActivity JOIN EntityWithAccessionedSequence e ON e.DB_ID = ca.physicalEntity JOIN ReferenceSequence rs ON rs.DB_ID = e.referenceEntity JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = rs.species AND d._displayName = 'Homo sapiens';

questions.question: How many distinct human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) have at least one recorded revision and have never been internally reviewed?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pw.DB_ID) FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN Event_2_revised rv ON rv.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_internalReviewed ir WHERE ir.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID);

questions.question: How many distinct events record at least one related species that is not also one of that same event's own species?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rs.DB_ID) FROM Event_2_relatedSpecies rs WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_species es WHERE es.DB_ID = rs.DB_ID AND es.species = rs.relatedSpecies);

questions.question: How many distinct human reaction-like events (species includes Homo sapiens) were inferred from an event that records a species other than Homo sapiens?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT inf.DB_ID) FROM Event_2_inferredFrom inf JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = inf.DB_ID JOIN Event_2_species hs ON hs.DB_ID = inf.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject h ON h.DB_ID = hs.species AND h._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_species es2 JOIN DatabaseObject d2 ON d2.DB_ID = es2.species WHERE es2.DB_ID = inf.inferredFrom AND d2._displayName <> 'Homo sapiens');

questions.question: How many distinct complexes record at least one included location that is not also one of that same complex's compartments?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT il.DB_ID) FROM Complex_2_includedLocation il WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Complex_2_compartment cc WHERE cc.DB_ID = il.DB_ID AND cc.compartment = il.includedLocation);

questions.question: For the human reaction-like events that have at least one catalyst activity, what is the mean catalytic rate constant (kcat) recorded for those catalyst activities?
Among the reference gene products referenced by EntityWithAccessionedSequence instances, which one has the greatest molecular mass in daltons?
Considering drugs whose reference therapeutic is marked as approved, what is the most frequently recorded recommended daily dosage?

Across human reaction-like events (species includes Homo sapiens), how many distinct pairings of an event with one of its compartments are recorded? Count each event-and-compartment pairing separately, so an event assigned three compartments contributes three pairings.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT rc.DB_ID, rc.compartment FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = rc.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens') t;

questions.question: For every species, count the distinct reaction-like events and the distinct pathways that record it as one of their species. Report the ten species with the most reaction-like events, ordered by that count descending and then by species name, using columns named species, reactions and pathways.

queries.sql: SELECT d._displayName AS species, COUNT(DISTINCT r.DB_ID) AS reactions, COUNT(DISTINCT pw.DB_ID) AS pathways FROM Event_2_species es JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = es.species LEFT JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = es.DB_ID LEFT JOIN Pathway pw ON pw.DB_ID = es.DB_ID GROUP BY es.species, d._displayName ORDER BY reactions DESC, species LIMIT 10;

questions.question: How many InstanceEdit instances are not recorded as the creating edit of any pathway? Treat a pathway as an instance of Pathway or of any subclass of Pathway.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM InstanceEdit ie WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Pathway pw JOIN DatabaseObject p ON p.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID AND p.created = ie.DB_ID);

questions.question: Treating the direct hasEvent children of the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 as depth 1, how many distinct events below that pathway are reachable at two or more different depths?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE lv AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev, 1 AS d FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent, lv.d + 1 FROM lv JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = lv.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT ev FROM lv GROUP BY ev HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d) > 1) t;

questions.question: The pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 has three direct hasEvent children. For each child, take the set of reaction-like events reachable from it through hasEvent at any depth. For every unordered pair of two different children, report the pair with columns pathway_a, pathway_b, shared and jaccard, where shared is the number of reaction-like events in both sets and jaccard is that number divided by the size of the union, rounded to four decimal places. Order by jaccard descending, then pathway_a, then pathway_b.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE roots AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS root FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256'), tree AS (SELECT root, root AS ev FROM roots UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM tree t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), rset AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, t.ev FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev), sizes AS (SELECT root, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rset GROUP BY root), inter AS (SELECT a.root AS ra, b.root AS rb, COUNT(*) AS k FROM rset a JOIN rset b ON b.ev = a.ev AND b.root > a.root GROUP BY a.root, b.root) SELECT da._displayName AS pathway_a, db2._displayName AS pathway_b, i.k AS shared, ROUND(i.k / (sa.n + sb.n - i.k), 4) AS jaccard FROM inter i JOIN sizes sa ON sa.root = i.ra JOIN sizes sb ON sb.root = i.rb JOIN DatabaseObject da ON da.DB_ID = i.ra JOIN DatabaseObject db2 ON db2.DB_ID = i.rb ORDER BY jaccard DESC, pathway_a, pathway_b;

questions.question: Rank species by the number of distinct reaction-like events that record them as one of their species, and take the top three. For each of those three, report the pathway that directly contains, through hasEvent, the greatest number of reaction-like events recording that species. Use columns species, pathway and reactions, ordered by reactions descending then species.

queries.sql: WITH sp3 AS (SELECT es.species AS sp, COUNT(DISTINCT es.DB_ID) AS n FROM Event_2_species es JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = es.DB_ID GROUP BY es.species ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 3), cnt AS (SELECT es.species AS sp, he.DB_ID AS pw, COUNT(DISTINCT he.hasEvent) AS n FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.hasEvent WHERE es.species IN (SELECT sp FROM sp3) GROUP BY es.species, he.DB_ID), rk AS (SELECT c.sp, c.pw, c.n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.sp ORDER BY c.n DESC, c.pw) AS r FROM cnt c) SELECT ds._displayName AS species, dp._displayName AS pathway, rk.n AS reactions FROM rk JOIN DatabaseObject ds ON ds.DB_ID = rk.sp JOIN DatabaseObject dp ON dp.DB_ID = rk.pw WHERE rk.r = 1 ORDER BY rk.n DESC, species;

questions.question: How many InstanceEdit instances that have D'Eustachio, Peter as one of their authors are not recorded as the creating edit of any pathway?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM InstanceEdit ie JOIN InstanceEdit_2_author ia ON ia.DB_ID = ie.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject p ON p.DB_ID = ia.author AND p._displayName = 'D''Eustachio, Peter' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Pathway pw JOIN DatabaseObject o ON o.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID AND o.created = ie.DB_ID);

questions.question: Human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) record an authored InstanceEdit, and each InstanceEdit records its own authors. Which person is an author of the authored InstanceEdit of the greatest number of distinct human pathways? Give the person's display name.

queries.sql: SELECT pe._displayName FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN Event_2_authored au ON au.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN InstanceEdit_2_author ia ON ia.DB_ID = au.authored JOIN DatabaseObject pe ON pe.DB_ID = ia.author GROUP BY ia.author, pe._displayName ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT pw.DB_ID) DESC LIMIT 1;

questions.question: The pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 has three direct hasEvent children. For each child, collect the physical entities that are a direct input to any reaction-like event reachable from that child through hasEvent at any depth. How many distinct physical entities appear in all three of those collections?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE roots AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS root FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256'), tree AS (SELECT root, root AS ev FROM roots UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM tree t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), ent AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, i.input AS e FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i ON i.DB_ID = t.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT e FROM ent GROUP BY e HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT root) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM roots)) x;

questions.question: How many human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) that directly contain at least one reaction-like event through hasEvent have the property that every one of those directly contained reaction-like events has at least one input and has every one of its inputs be a Complex?

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT he.DB_ID) FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent h2 JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r2 ON r2.DB_ID = h2.hasEvent WHERE h2.DB_ID = he.DB_ID AND (NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i WHERE i.DB_ID = h2.hasEvent) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i WHERE i.DB_ID = h2.hasEvent AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Complex cx WHERE cx.DB_ID = i.input))));

questions.question: For each human pathway (species includes Homo sapiens) whose hasEvent subtree contains at least one reaction-like event, count those distinct reaction-like events. Divide the pathways into four equally sized groups by that count using NTILE ordered ascending, and report how many pathways fall in the highest group.

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS root, he.hasEvent AS ev FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), agg AS (SELECT t.root, COUNT(DISTINCT t.ev) AS n FROM t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = t.ev GROUP BY t.root), q AS (SELECT root, n, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY n) AS tile FROM agg) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM q WHERE tile = 4;

questions.question: Starting from the pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256, repeatedly follow either a hasEvent link from a pathway to a contained event or a precedingEvent link from an event to an event that precedes it, in any order and any number of times. How many distinct reaction-like events are reachable?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE reach AS (SELECT he.hasEvent AS ev FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier s ON s.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' UNION SELECT he.hasEvent FROM reach r JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = r.ev UNION SELECT p.precedingEvent FROM reach r JOIN Event_2_precedingEvent p ON p.DB_ID = r.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reach JOIN ReactionlikeEvent x ON x.DB_ID = reach.ev;

questions.question: For each of the pathways with stable identifiers R-HSA-168249, R-HSA-1280218 and R-HSA-1280215, collect the physical entities that are a direct input to any reaction-like event reachable from it through hasEvent at any depth. How many distinct physical entities are in both the R-HSA-168249 collection and the R-HSA-1280218 collection while not being in the R-HSA-1280215 collection?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (SELECT s.identifier AS root, he.hasEvent AS ev FROM StableIdentifier s JOIN DatabaseObject o ON o.stableIdentifier = s.DB_ID JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = o.DB_ID WHERE s.identifier IN ('R-HSA-168249','R-HSA-1280218','R-HSA-1280215') UNION SELECT t.root, he.hasEvent FROM tree t JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = t.ev), ent AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.root, i.input AS e FROM tree t JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_input i ON i.DB_ID = t.ev) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT e FROM ent WHERE root = 'R-HSA-168249') a JOIN (SELECT e FROM ent WHERE root = 'R-HSA-1280218') b ON b.e = a.e WHERE a.e NOT IN (SELECT e FROM ent WHERE root = 'R-HSA-1280215');

questions.question: How many human pathways (species includes Homo sapiens) directly contain, through hasEvent, at least one reaction-like event that is not reachable through hasEvent at any depth from any pathway that the same human pathway also directly contains?

queries.sql: WITH RECURSIVE cp AS (SELECT c.DB_ID AS p, c.hasEvent AS ch FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent c JOIN Pathway x ON x.DB_ID = c.hasEvent), desc_ AS (SELECT cp.p, cp.ch AS node FROM cp UNION SELECT d.p, he.hasEvent FROM desc_ d JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent he ON he.DB_ID = d.node) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT he.DB_ID) FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM desc_ d WHERE d.p = he.DB_ID AND d.node = he.hasEvent);
